reason: The prospect as recorded does not exist. 'Omterra' is the new corporate brand of Siemens Energy ITSELF (and Siemens Gamesa), announced 14 Jul 2026 because the Siemens brand licence from the 2020 spin-off is time-limited; rebranding rolls out in stages from later in 2026. The carve-out is a different thing: on 25 Aug 2026 Siemens Energy's supervisory board approved the legal and operational separation of its Transformation of Industry business area (steam turbines, compressors, electrolysers; ~17,000 employees; ~EUR 5.7B revenue in fiscal 2025; Q3 FY26 revenue EUR 1.5B at 14.3% margin), with options ranging from external investors to a capital-markets transaction and Siemens Energy retaining a significant minority stake; Bloomberg-reported value above EUR 10B; CVC, EQT, Bain, Brookfield and KKR reported as interested. That unit has NO announced name, NO announced chief executive or leadership team of its own, NO brand and NO decided structure (IPO or private-equity sale), so the verified named decision-maker and decision path the standard requires cannot exist yet; the only people to call today are Siemens Energy's board (CEO Christian Bruch) and Anne-Laure de Chammard, listed on Siemens Energy board profiles as Executive Vice President for Transformation of Industry — confirm she leads the carve-out before any contact. Two category hazards for whenever it does surface: on the Formula E side ABB, the championship's title partner, is a direct electrification and grid rival; on the F1 side Siemens AG (a separate company since 2020) is the FIA's Official Digital Twin Sponsor and a McLaren and Ferrari partner, an adjacency the desk must not conflate with the prospect. The Versigent archetype is right and the catalyst is real, so put it on the catalyst radar: re-surface when the carve-out has a name, a CEO and a transaction structure, at which point the born-big spin-off case (new brand from zero, EUR 5.7B revenue) is worth building properly, most likely for F1 given the ABB clash in Formula E.
